audit.whatIsWrong: mid claims Feast is a "percentage-current-health nuke" and that "your grey-health stack actually makes his R hit harder in absolute terms". whys[5] repeats it: "your first item sustain loop has no answer for percentage-current-health damage".
audit.why: This is the most damaging error I found in the whole slice, because it does not just misdescribe an ability — it tells a Tahm Kench player that his core build makes him MORE vulnerable, which is exactly backwards. Feast deals flat true damage that scales with Cho'Gath's own bonus health and AP. It does not scale with the target's current or maximum health in any way. Every point of HP Tahm Kench stacks is strictly good against Feast. A player who believes this line will drop Heartsteel and Warmog's from the build against the one matchup where raw HP is cleanly correct.
audit.corrected: Feast is flat true damage keyed to HIS bonus health, not yours. Stack HP freely; it never feeds his ultimate.
sources: champ-data/_kits/chogath.json (R: "Devours an enemy unit, dealing a high amount of true damage" — no percentage clause)
League of Legends Wiki — Cho'Gath (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Cho%27Gath/LoL) — "Champion True Damage: 300/475/650 (+50% AP) (+10% bonus health)", the bonus health being Cho'Gath's own

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] says Feast "does true damage that pierces your Thick Skin grey health"; whys[6] says it "executes you through any amount of Thick Skin grey health".
audit.why: True damage ignores armour and magic resist. It does not ignore shields — Thick Skin's converted shield absorbs it like any other damage. Two separate strings tell the reader their defensive ability does not function against his ultimate, which will make them hold E rather than convert.
audit.corrected: True damage bypasses resistances, not shields.
sources: League of Legends Wiki — Cho'Gath (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Cho%27Gath/LoL) — shields listed as blocking Feast damage
champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (E: "Convert all stored damage into a temporary shield")

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] states "His Rupture and Feral Scream cooldowns are long enough that a clean Q-into-stun-into-Devour removes him from the wave".
audit.why: Rupture is 6 seconds at EVERY rank — it does not scale down because it starts short. There is no long cooldown window to punish; you dodge it and it is back almost immediately. Building a level-3 plan around a punish window that does not exist is how a player walks into the knockup they were told they had time to avoid.
audit.corrected: Rupture is 6s flat at all ranks; the window is one dodge wide, not a rotation.
sources: League of Legends Wiki — Cho'Gath (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Cho%27Gath/LoL) — Rupture cooldown 6 at all ranks

audit.whatIsWrong: early says "his Feral Scream silence interrupts your Devour mid-cast"; whys[1] says it "can silence your Devour mid-cast".
audit.why: A silence prevents you from starting a cast; it does not interrupt one already committed. The practical advice barely changes but the mechanic stated does, and the file uses precise CC language elsewhere. The correct read is that you must check his W before you spend stacks, not that he can rip a Devour out of the air.
audit.corrected: Silence stops you starting the cast — check it before committing, not during.

audit.whatIsWrong: early claims Rupture's knockup "resets your An Acquired Taste count".
audit.why: Nothing in either kit supports a CC-triggered stack reset. An Acquired Taste stacks are built by damaging the champion and fall off over time; being knocked up does not zero them. The real cost of eating Rupture is the tempo — you stop applying damage, so the stacks time out.
audit.corrected: Reworded to the effect that is actually true: it costs the exchange and buys time for the stacks to decay.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (P: "Damaging enemy champions builds stacks" — no reset condition)

audit.whatIsWrong: Carnivore is never mentioned, and the entry's early-game plan is built on grinding him down with poke.
audit.why: Cho'Gath recovers health AND mana on every unit he kills, scaling with level. He is one of the few top laners who simply farms his way out of a poke war, which means the "win the short-trade war levels 1-3" plan in wants.you[2] has no closing mechanism. Denying him CS is the actual lever.
audit.corrected: Named in wants.you[0], with denying CS as the consequence.
sources: champ-data/_kits/chogath.json (P: "Whenever Cho'Gath kills a unit, he recovers Health and Mana")

audit.whatIsWrong: mid and late route the map plan through "Abyssal Voyage", and early says "never commit the W without confirming his W is on cooldown" while plainly meaning Devour.
audit.why: Both are artifacts of Tahm Kench's pre-rework kit, where Devour was W and Abyssal Voyage was R. On the current kit W is Abyssal Dive and Devour is R. The "commit the W" phrasing is a useful tell that this text was written against the old kit and never revalidated.
audit.corrected: Abyssal Dive for the blink, Devour named as the thing you commit.
sources: League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench)

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0], early and whys[2] run the "Q-into-Devour" / "3-stack stun into Devour" pattern.
audit.why: The Q stun at 3 stacks consumes all three stacks and Devour requires 3 stacks. One payoff per cycle.
audit.corrected: Three stacks buys the stun or the eat, chosen before you commit.
sources: League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench)

audit.whatIsWrong: The content-layer level chart gives Cho'Gath five of seven stages and the prose is openly defeatist — "do not 1v1 him", "the 1v1 is over", "an unkillable frontliner". The packet win rate is 52.92% in Tahm Kench's favour over 616 games, and the FULL layer disagrees too: diff EVEN, four of seven phases to Tahm Kench, Cho'Gath carry threat only 7/10.
audit.why: Here the content layer is the outlier rather than the full layer — the reverse of the Aatrox and Cassiopeia entries. A reader is being told to concede a lane the data says they win slightly more often than not, and much of the pessimism rests on the Feast misdescription corrected above.
audit.corrected: I softened the claims that were also factually wrong (the Feast cluster) but did not touch the chart itself — win[] champion names cannot change length enough to swap inside the +/-10% band. Flagged in notes.

audit.why: I checked Rupture's "grounding" flag in champ-data/_kits/chogath.json and did not use it. Riot's text for Rupture is "popping enemy units into the air, dealing damage and slowing them" — knockup and slow, no grounding. The flag looks like another bad derivation, similar to the spurious grounding flags on Ambessa's W and R. Notably Rupture is NOT flagged knockup despite plainly knocking up, so the flag block for this champion is unreliable in both directions.
audit.corrected: No grounding advice written for Rupture.
sources: champ-data/_kits/chogath.json (Q flags: grounding, slow, zone — grounding unsupported by the description, knockup missing from it)

edits.before: This lane opens even because Cho'Gath is legitimately dangerous from level 1 — his Rupture hitbox is wide, and if it knocks you up while you are fishing for Tongue Lash stacks it resets your An Acquired Taste count and puts you on the back foot. Walk perpendicular to his Rupture to bait it, then immediately step up with Q to begin stacking. The 3-stack stun into Devour is your threat: if he disrespects your slow and waddles forward without dodging Q, you punish him hard. The bad news is that at level 2 his Feral Scream silence interrupts your Devour mid-cast, so never commit the W without confirming his W is on cooldown. Farm patiently through the first few levels and accept that short trades favor him if he lands Rupture.
edits.after: This lane opens even because Cho'Gath is legitimately dangerous from level 1 — his Rupture hitbox is wide, and if it knocks you up while you are fishing for Tongue Lash stacks it costs you the exchange and buys time for your An Acquired Taste stacks to fall off. Walk perpendicular to his Rupture to bait it, then immediately step up with Q to begin stacking. Three stacks is the threat: it buys the Tongue Lash stun or a Devour, never both, so pick before you commit. The bad news is that his Feral Scream silence stops you starting Devour at all, so never commit without confirming his W is on cooldown. Farm patiently through the first few levels and accept that short trades favour him if he lands Rupture.

edits.before: Level 6 is where this lane shifts against you for good, not for you — Cho'Gath's Feast does true damage that bypasses Thick Skin entirely, and his percentage-current-health nuke means your grey-health stack actually makes his R hit harder in absolute terms. From here you are fishing for the punish window around his Rupture and Feral Scream cooldowns, not hunting the all-in. Use Abyssal Voyage to contribute to skirmishes elsewhere and return to lane healthy rather than bleeding chip damage trying to force a kill he can just R you out of. Dodge Rupture, hold your E activation to shield after Feral Scream ends, and reset to base when your grey health is high but not yet banked.
edits.after: Level 6 shifts the lane, but not the way this used to read — Feast is flat true damage that scales with his own bonus health and AP, never with yours, so every point of HP you stack is strictly good against it. What true damage ignores is armour and MR, not Thick Skin's shield. From here you are fishing for the punish window around his Rupture and Feral Scream cooldowns, not hunting the all-in. Use Abyssal Dive to contribute to skirmishes elsewhere and return to lane healthy rather than bleeding chip damage trying to force a kill. Dodge Rupture, hold your E activation to shield after Feral Scream ends, and reset to base when your grey health is high but not yet banked.

edits.before: At two or more items Cho'Gath's Feast stacks have turned him into a wall of HP your kit has no answer for — your Devour combo still displaces him for a moment but you cannot follow it up with enough damage to matter, and his R true-damage execute threatens you even through full Heartsteel scaling. Your job pivots entirely to peeling your own carries with Devour and using Abyssal Voyage to be the first body on objectives. Never duel him without your team; the 1v1 is over.
edits.after: At two or more items Cho'Gath's Feast stacks have turned him into a wall of HP your damage cannot chew through — Devour still removes him from a fight, but you will not kill him alone. Feast itself is one 80s cast at 175 range that scales off his bonus health, not yours, so Heartsteel stays exactly right. Your job pivots to peeling your own carries with Devour and using Abyssal Dive to be the first body on objectives. Duel him for the wave, not for the kill.

edits.after: Cho'Gath's Feast comes up — flat true damage at 175 range on an 80s cooldown, so it ignores armour and MR but never scales off your health.

edits.before: At 2+ items Feast stacks make Cho'Gath a near-unkillable frontliner whose true-damage R ignores every point of your sustain — do not 1v1 him.
edits.after: At 2+ items Feast stacks make Cho'Gath a durable frontliner, but his R is one 80s cast at melee range — respect it, then keep trading.

edits.after: Lick Cho'Gath to 3 stacks in short exchanges, then spend them once — Devour his all-in under your own wave.

notes:
HIGHEST-PRIORITY FIX IN MY WHOLE SLICE is in this entry. mid and whys[5] told the reader that Feast is a "percentage-current-health nuke" and that "your grey-health stack actually makes his R hit harder in absolute terms". That is backwards. Feast is flat true damage scaling with CHO'GATH'S bonus health and AP, never the target's. The old text actively argued a Tahm Kench player out of stacking HP in a matchup where stacking HP is unambiguously correct. Two more strings (spikes[1], whys[6]) claimed Feast "pierces" Thick Skin's grey health — true damage bypasses resistances, not shields.

LAYER DISAGREEMENT, opposite direction to my other entries: here the CONTENT layer is the pessimistic outlier. Its chart gives Cho'Gath five of seven stages and the prose says "do not 1v1 him" and "the 1v1 is over", while the win rate is 52.92% over 616 games and the full layer independently says diff EVEN, four of seven phases to Tahm Kench, Cho'Gath carry threat 7/10. Much of the content layer's pessimism was resting on the Feast error above, so it should be re-read now that the mechanic is stated correctly. I could not touch win[] entries — champion names cannot swap inside the +/-10% length band.

DATA CONFLICT worth resolving upstream: champ-data/_kits/chogath.json gives Feral Scream range 300; the League Wiki gives 650 edge range. Data Dragon appears to report the cast range rather than the cone length for this ability. I cited NEITHER number in any edit rather than pick one. The same caution probably applies to other cone abilities in the kit library.

FLAG DERIVATION UNRELIABLE FOR THIS CHAMPION IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: Rupture carries a "grounding" flag it should not have (it knocks up and slows), and is missing the "knockup" flag it obviously should have. Feast carries a "percentHealth" flag that most likely produced the error at the top of these notes — the percentage in Feast's text refers to Cho'Gath's own health growth, not the target's.

Legacy-kit tell: early says "never commit the W" while meaning Devour. On the pre-rework kit Devour WAS the W and Abyssal Voyage was the R. Combined with the 182 "Abyssal Voyage" occurrences across this file, it looks like a large amount of this content was written against the old Tahm Kench kit and never revalidated.
